function_identity.rule: Same exact head, same unknown partial function; different heads may alias

assumptions: Operation-selection versus execution split is newly proposed, not observed word meaning.
One shared state type and partial endofunction typing for the selected heads.
Same descriptor fixes operation identity; no particular transformation or state value chosen.
Local head lookup is pure and adjacent outputs feed later inputs.
Every repeated DAIIN contributes one application event; none silently deleted.
Finite bound expansions only; known different-reader splits/annotations retained.
Source order used within safe interpreted spans, not invented whole-page process chronology.
All143groups preserved,123outside operation spans unexecuted; no global execution or final-state claim.

limits.types: One abstract state domain S; each selected complete descriptor X supplies one unknown partial F_X:S->S. Partiality permits operation preconditions and undefined composition; no silent totality assumption.
limits.step: If F_X(s) is defined, append an application event and set current state to its output. Otherwise the proposed run is not executable at that input.
limits.same_form: The same whole descriptor denotes the same F_X in every selected construction; different written descriptors may denote the same actual function. DOL and DAL strings remain distinct; no assumed functional inequality.
limits.two_applications: F_X(F_X(s)), not two unrelated calls from s. Two calls do not require two effects or different final states.
limits.two_heads: F_Y(F_X(s)); reversed order gives F_X(F_Y(s)), but noncommutation is not guaranteed for unknown functions.
limits.finite_fusion: LicensedXdaiin is one F_X application, with one source group retained. This remains a finite writing hypothesis, not confirmed morpheme identity.
limits.unread_intervals: No state threading through unread intervening text or unresolved source boundaries. Each subsequent local chain has an unbound boundary-state input, not a claimed reset/refill/no-op.
limits.resources: No resource instance is created by the parser or by a new source name. A selected operation may have unknown physical effects; none is assigned. Old R_TOKEN remains invalid for its own fixed resource-consuming semantics.
limits.old_anchors: All five Q2 source-anchor sites are preserved as prior-interpretation provenance only, not active resource identities in EXEC. Function choice uses the head descriptor, so latest-mention choice no longer decides it. This gives up those semantic obligations; it is not an empirical improvement. Four old marker relations remain uninterpreted.
